- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate mean — adjust downward by 2–5% of recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending up, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — reduce forecast slope by 15–20% in 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates volatility — use 10-day rolling standard deviation to cap forecast deviation from mean by ±1.5σ.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending down, model often ignores sentiment — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day of positive sentiment.
- When sentiment is negative and price is near support, model often fails to recognize reversal — add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid undershoot.
